note: WHAT THIS WORK COSTS EVERYWHERE ELSE. Research, not a price list. Nothing in this file is a McCluster price; data/offers.json is the only place a McCluster price lives. This exists so the desk can put a real number beside its own when somebody asks 'is that cheap or not', which is the question behind almost every price question.
stale_line: These are the figures as of the date checked. Market rates move; if the checked date is more than six months old, say the number is from a guide rather than from this week.
what_these_numbers_are: Ranges published in 2026 pricing guides for small-business work in these markets and nationally. They are NOT quotes from named local companies, they are NOT what any particular competitor charges, and they must never be presented as either.
how_to_use_it: State the band, then state the McCluster price, and stop. Let them do the subtraction.
Never say 'cheaper than everyone' or 'the lowest price'. Some of these prices are not below the band, and a claim that is wrong once is a claim nobody believes again.
Never name a competitor and never attribute a price to one.
A band is a band. Do not quote the midpoint as if it were a fact about a specific business.

rates.label: A small-business website, built
rates.detail: Freelancers $1,500–$8,000. Agencies $5,000–$30,000. A basic site for a local service business in New Haven starts around $1,500–$4,500; Atlanta small-business projects land $2,000–$10,000.

rates.label: Hosting and maintenance
rates.detail: Freelancers $50–$200/mo. Agencies $150–$500/mo. Connecticut packages commonly $50–$325/mo. Yearly, that is $1,000–$6,000 for a small-business site.

rates.label: Social media management, on its own
rates.detail: 44% of small businesses spend $500–$2,000/mo. Boutique agencies $1,000–$4,000/mo for two or three platforms. Full done-for-you work commonly $2,500/mo. This band is for SOCIAL ALONE, with no website management in it.

rates.label: A professional headshot session
rates.detail: One to two hours, three to ten retouched images.

rates.label: Event photography
rates.detail: Event photographers charge $150-$500 an hour. This rate was $310 — inside the band rather than under it — until the golden discount was applied; it is now at the ceiling.

rates.label: A photography half-day
rates.unit: up to four or five hours
rates.detail: For smaller projects a half-day of four to five hours runs $800-$2,000. This rate was $2,210, ABOVE the band, until the golden discount brought it to the ceiling. It is the one price on this list that had to come down rather than already being under.

rates.label: A photography full day
rates.detail: A full day runs $1,500-$4,000 for smaller projects. Experienced commercial and advertising photographers run $3,000-$10,000 for the photographer alone, before studio, models, styling or retouching.

rates.label: A produced video day
rates.detail: Compared against the PRODUCED tier, not a bare freelance videographer at $600-$1,200 a day, because these days include the kit, the crew and the edit. A minimal five-person crew starts near $2,400 for one shoot day; a full crew is $3,000-$8,000.

rates.label: A produced video half-day
rates.detail: Half-days run 60-70% of a full day rather than half, which is why the band is not simply the day band halved.

rates.label: A music video
rates.detail: Shoestring shoots $2,000-$5,000. A professionally produced music video averages $5,000-$30,000. Commercial productions go far past that and are not the comparison here.

rates.label: A brand film
rates.detail: A produced 60-second brand video runs $15,000-$75,000; brand films and multi-day productions $20,000-$50,000.

golden_discount.what_it_means: Nothing here costs more than 67% of the market median for the same work. The ceiling is a CEILING and not a target: a price already below it is left alone rather than raised up to it. Raising the cheap end to hit a discount number exactly would put the price up on the people this discount exists to reach, and would end the free build, which is the hook the whole offer rests on.
golden_discount.the_claim_this_supports: At least a third below what this work costs around here. True of every line, because any line that was not true of was moved until it was.
golden_discount.recompute: node scripts/golden-check.mjs — re-derives every ceiling from this file and fails if the ledger drifts above one. Run it after any change to a median or a price.
